subject: Sequencing GPU Rosters for LyraAnalytics Dedicated Deployment
messages:
From: Jae Park <jae.park@lyraanalytics.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity planning: Dedicated deployment timing & roster

Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an internal board meeting on Feb 25 and need a concrete plan for the Dedicated deployment timeline and how you’ll roster GPU capacity for LyraAnalytics. High-level asks:

- Target go-live: mid-April (hard constraint from our product roadmap)
- Expected steady-state: ~80 concurrent API sessions, median request payload ~1k tokens, peaks up to 4k tokens
- Models: mixture of 30B and 70B variants (we plan to quantize some slices)

Can you send a proposed phasing plan (which windows get reserved vs burst), estimated number of 80GB A100 / H100 equivalents needed over time, and what protection against noisy neighbors / preemption you can guarantee?

I’ll loop in Angela (ops) on scheduling and any compliance questions.

Thanks,
Jae
Jae Park
Head of ML Platforms | LyraAnalytics

(attachment: Lyra_expected_workload.xlsx)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Jae Park <jae.park@lyraanalytics.com>
Cc: Angela Morris <angela@lyraanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity planning: Dedicated deployment timing & roster

Jae —

Great to hear the board timeline. Quick confirmation questions so we size correctly:

- Is 80 concurrent sessions your peak at roll-out or steady-state?
- Percent of traffic that is low-latency (<=150ms) vs batch-tolerant?
- Any hard constraint on model versions being pinned vs accepting a compatible variant for availability?

Initial thinking (very high level):
- Phase 1 (canary, 2–4 weeks): reserve a baseline of capacity sized for 25 concurrent sessions with guaranteed low-latency SLOs (A100/H100 equivalent pool).
- Phase 2 (ramp, 4–8 weeks): add scheduled reserved windows and burst quotas to reach ~60–80 concurrent.
- Phase 3 (steady): convert to a committed dedicated pool per SOW, with autoscaling on top for transient spikes.

I’m attaching the workbook you sent and will circulate a more formal projection after a quick infra scoping call tomorrow.

Connor OBrien
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Lyra_expected_workload.xlsx)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning: Dedicated deployment timing & roster

Connor —

Spoke with infra and did a quick projection based on Jae’s numbers. Key technical notes for the proposal:

- Model sizing: 30B -> ~A100 40GB equivalent per nice-to-have instance; 70B -> ~A100 80GB / H100 equivalence. Given token sizes, assume 70B will dominate GPU RAM for long sequences.
- Throughput estimates (conservative): a single 80GB equiv GPU can sustain ~10 reqs/sec at 1k tokens (with batching and KV cache). For 80 concurrent, target sustained capacity ~8–10 GPUs if sessions are short; for long 4k-token sessions plan ~18–22 GPUs.
- Options to reduce footprint: 4-bit quantization on the 30B slice, A/B serving for larger models (route low-latency requests to scaled 30B variants).
- Contention handling: we can implement a soft-guarantee + preemption window. Reserved baseline (no preemption) + burst pool (best-effort) is the clearest offering for customers who need predictable low-latency.

Proposal we should present to Lyra:
1) Reserve baseline of 6x80GB equiv for Phase 1 (canary) — covers low-latency 25 concurrent.
2) Schedule ramp to 12x80GB equiv over 6 weeks, using reserved windows (guaranteed) + assigned burst quota (best-effort) to hit 80 concurrent at peaks.
3) Provide documented preemption SLAs and an incident rollback plan (fallback to smaller model variants automatically).

I’ve attached a quick projection PDF. We should also surface cost delta vs a fully reserved pool so they can trade latency vs price.

karthik
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
(attachment: capacity_projection_v1.pdf)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning: Dedicated deployment timing & roster

Connor / Karthik —

Flag: we have an existing reserved commitment for HelixCo in early April that overlaps with Lyra’s mid-April go-live window. HelixCo’s SOW included hard reserved windows for 10x80GB equiv capacity for April 1–21. If Lyra needs guaranteed reserved capacity starting mid-April we will have to either:

- Re-schedule HelixCo (expensive and politically sensitive), or
- Use burst/reservation split and guarantee Lyra a smaller non-preemptible baseline with a firm ramp schedule, or
- Escalate to execs for one-off re-prioritization if Lyra’s ARR/contract warrants it.

Connor — can you confirm Lyra’s tolerance for a phased baseline + burst plan vs a full reserved carveout? If they request full reserved windows that match HelixCo we should flag for leadership.

Hannah
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com; connor_obrien@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning: Dedicated deployment timing & roster

All —

I don’t want to re-run full execs for this yet. Proposed prioritization framework (applies when two deals want the same reserved windows):

- Priority 1: Signed commitment with payment + legal SOW specifying reserved windows (hard contractual obligation).
- Priority 2: Deals with binding purchase orders or near-term invoice schedules (>3 months ARR equivalent) where customer accepts phased reservation (we offer credits if guaranteed windows are shifted).
- Priority 3: Pre-sales or non-binding pilots; move to burst/scheduled canary.

Applying that to HelixCo vs Lyra: HelixCo has an existing SOW for April (Priority 1). Lyra is currently in negotiation (we have term sheet, not signed SOW) — Priority 2. Recommendation: offer Lyra a firm phased plan:

- Baseline guaranteed carveout of 6x80GB equiv starting Apr 15 for 2 weeks (no preemption).
- Additional 6x80GB equiv available as burst capacity (best-effort) with a documented ramp schedule to convert burst into reserved capacity upon SOW signature within 45 days.
- Provide Lyra a billing credit if we must shift any scheduled reserved windows beyond the committed ramp due to higher-priority contracts.

This keeps HelixCo’s contract intact, gives Lyra predictability for go-live, and creates a clear conversion trigger (signature + payment) for more capacity. Connor — please propose language in the SOW and a DocuSign timeline; include the credit terms as a protected clause.

Marissa Cole
Head of GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
(attachment: dedicated_sow_draft.docx)

Subject: Plan & next steps: phased roster for mid-April go-live

Jae / Angela —

Appreciate the prompt answers and patience while we surfaced internal commitments. Summary of what we can offer for your mid-April go-live: 

- Guaranteed baseline: 6x80GB-equivalent GPUs available Apr 15–Apr 30 (non-preemptible).
- Burst pool: additional 6x80GB-equivalent available best-effort for spikes; we’ll throttle if higher-priority reserved windows need capacity.
- Ramp to full reserved pool: upon signed SOW (LYR-2026-0127) and initial payment within 45 days we convert burst to reserved capacity and schedule dedicated windows.
- Contention protection: automatic fallback routing to quantized 30B variants and documented preemption SLA; we’ll provide a runbook for degradation modes.

Next steps: I’ll send the SOW draft with the DocuSign link today (includes the credit formula if reserved windows are shifted). Please review and let me know if we should schedule a short call Friday to lock timelines.

Connor OBrien
